<ns0:div xmlns:ns0="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12" type="chapter">
               <ns0:head>CHAP. XII.</ns0:head>
               <ns0:p n="1">1 IN the mean time, when there were gathered together an innumerable multitude of people, insomuch that they trode one upon another, he be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gan to say unto his disciples first of all, Beware ye of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />crisie.<ns0:note place="bottom">We read of such a caution given to the Disciples, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 16.6. But that is not the same caution with this; there he compared their <ns0:hi>Doctrine</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>Leaven,</ns0:hi> for the aptness of it to infect others, here he compareth their Lives to the same thing<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and for the same reason; this appeareth to be the same Sense of our Saviour here, because he saith their Leaven is <ns0:hi>Hypocrisy.</ns0:hi> There are none so like to do mischief to the better sort of People, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> those that under a Mask, and Exterior Di<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>guise of severity and strict<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness, indulge themselves in Corrupt Affections, and Vitious In<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />clinations.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="2">2 For there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; neither hid, that shall not be known.<ns0:note place="bottom">It is a <ns0:hi>Proverbial Expression,</ns0:hi> those, and Parabolical Expressi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ons, may be applyed in several Cases, and to several Subjects; we have met with this before variously applyed, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 10.26. <ns0:hi>Mar.</ns0:hi> 4.22. and in this Gospel, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 8.17. Here it is applyed, as an Argument against <ns0:hi>Hypocrisy,</ns0:hi> or the concealing of naugh<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ty and Corrupt Hearts under the Vizor, and Disguise of demure Looks, or fair Conversation. In the Day of Judgment, Sinners shall walk <ns0:hi>Naked,</ns0:hi> and Men shall see their Shame; God will in that Day make known all the Secrets of Mens Hearts, to be sure the secrets of all their Hearts, whose Iniquities are not forgi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven, and whose Sins are not covered.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="3">3 Therefore whatsoever ye have spoken in darkness, shall be heard in the light, and that which ye have spoken in the ear in closets, shall be proclaim<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed upon the house-tops.<ns0:note place="bottom">We have something very like this, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 10.27. spoken by way of Precept. It seemeth to be a Sentence also variously applyed; it may be left indifferent to the <ns0:hi>Reader,</ns0:hi> whether he will under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stand it as a promise of the <ns0:hi>Publication of the Gospel</ns0:hi> (to which purpose it seems to be spoken in the form of a Precept, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 10.27.) or as a further enlargement of his former Discourse, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 2.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="4">4 And I say unto my friends, Be not afraid of them that kill the body, and after that, have no more that they can do:</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">5 But I will forewarn you whom you shall fear, Fear him, which after he hath killed, hath power to cast into hell, yea, I say unto you, Fear him.<ns0:note place="bottom">See the Notes on <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 10.28. where we met with the same, from this to the 13. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> our Saviour Armeth his Disciples, to encounter those storms of Persecution, which he knew they would meet with after he should be taken up into Heaven. Here are two Arguments in this Verse, 1. The one drawn from the <ns0:hi>Impotency,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Limited Power</ns0:hi> of the most Malicious Enemies; they can <ns0:hi>Kill the Body,</ns0:hi> but can do no more, 2. From <ns0:hi>the migh<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ty Power of God,</ns0:hi> who <ns0:hi>can cast us into Hell, Matthew</ns0:hi> saith, who c<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>n <ns0:hi>cast Body and Soul into Hell Fire</ns0:hi>: Whence is evident, 1. That there are punishments beyond this Life, all Mens Punish<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ments will not end with the killing of their Bodies, 2. That Men have <ns0:hi>Soul<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>,</ns0:hi> as well as <ns0:hi>Bodies,</ns0:hi> and both Souls and Bodies of Sinners will in the Resurrection<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> be made capable of Eternal Pu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nishment. 3. That the ready way to bring us under that Misery, is to be more afraid of the wrath of Men than of the wrath of God.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">6 Are not five sparrows sold for two farthings, and not one of them is forgotten before God?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">7 But even the very hairs of your head are all numbred. Fear not therefore, ye are of more value then many sparrows.<ns0:note place="bottom">See the Notes on <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 10.29, 30, 31. Our Saviours third Argument is brought from the Providence of God, both his <ns0:hi>Ge<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />neral Providence</ns0:hi> upholding the Beings of all his Creatures, so that he forg<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>tteth not a <ns0:hi>Sparrow,</ns0:hi> tho a Creature of so minute a value, that two of them are sold for a Farthing (as <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> saith) or <ns0:hi>Five</ns0:hi> for two Farthings (as <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> saith) yea, he so re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />membreth them, that one of them falls not to the Ground with<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />out his knowledge and leave, saith <ns0:hi>Matthew.</ns0:hi> But besides this, God exerciseth a more special Providence towards Creatures; with reference to their Dignity, and Excellency now (saith our Saviour) you are of more value than many Sparrows, you are so as <ns0:hi>Men,</ns0:hi> you are more so as my Disciples, especially as my Ministers and Embassadors. <ns0:hi>The very Hairs of your Head are numbred,</ns0:hi> God will regard your most minute concerns.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">2 Tim. 2.12</ns0:note> Also I say unto you, Whosoever shall con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fess me before men, him shall the Son of man also con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fess before the angels of God.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 But he that denieth me before men, shall be de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nied before the angels of God.<ns0:note place="bottom">See the Notes on <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 10.32, 33. Here is a fourth and fifth Argument, drawn from the <ns0:hi>Rewards,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Punishments</ns0:hi> of such as shall confess, or deny Christ before Men. <ns0:hi>Confession</ns0:hi> here sig<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nifies, The owning, and adhering to the Truths, and Ways of God, in a time of Opposition; the Reward promised, is, Christs own<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing those that do it at the Day of Judgment; before <ns0:hi>the Father</ns0:hi> (saith <ns0:hi>Matthew) before the Angels,</ns0:hi> saith <ns0:hi>Luke.</ns0:hi> Christ hath no need of our owning him, his truth and ways; we may by it be profitable to our selves, but not to him, we shall have need in the Day of Judgment of Christs owning us. By the denial of Christ, is meant our Apostacy from the Truths, or ways of God, the <ns0:hi>denial</ns0:hi> of his truths, ways, or interest in this World it implys a Persecuting of them<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> but signifyeth something much less, a denial by words, or a forsaking and not adhering to them. The punishment will be Christs <ns0:hi>denial</ns0:hi> of us in the Day of Judgment. What that sig<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nifyeth <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> tells us, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 7. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 23. <ns0:hi>I will profess unto them,</ns0:hi> I never knew you. Depart from me, I know you not, ye workers of Iniqui<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ty; and <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 25, 41. he shall say <ns0:hi>to them on his left Hand, Depart from me ye Cursed into Everlasting Fire, prepared for the Devil and his Angels.</ns0:hi> This must be understood not of such as <ns0:hi>deny him,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> did, in an House of great Temptation, and then go out and <ns0:hi>Weep bitterly,</ns0:hi> and again return unto him, but of such as Persist in such denials, and return not to confess him.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 And whosoever shall speak a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him, but unto him that blasphemeth against the holy Ghost, it shall not be forgiven.<ns0:note place="bottom">See the Notes on <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 12.31. and on <ns0:hi>Mar.</ns0:hi> 3.29.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 And when they bring you unto the synagogues, and <ns0:hi>unto</ns0:hi> magistrates, and powers, take ye no thought how or what thing ye shall answer, or what ye shall say.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 For the holy Ghost shall teach you in the same hour, what ye ought to say.<ns0:note place="bottom">See the <ns0:hi>Notes</ns0:hi> on <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 10.19. <ns0:hi>Mar.</ns0:hi> 13.11.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 And one of the company said unto him, Master, speak to my brother, that he divide the inheritance with me.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 And he said unto him, Man, who made me a judge, or a divider over you.<ns0:note place="bottom">This Passage certainly is not recorded for nothing, if it teach<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth us any thing, it is this, <ns0:hi>That matters of Civil Iustice belong not to those whom Christ sends to Preach his Gospel.</ns0:hi> That Work is enough for them: Christ here refuseth the Office so much as of an Arbitrator. A very learned Author tells us, that the practice of bringing Civil Matters before Ecclesiastical Men, as Judges began in the <ns0:hi>Captivity of Babylon,</ns0:hi> the Jews by that means avoiding the bringing their differences before Pagan Judges, which the Apostle also persuadeth at large to the Primitive Christians, in 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 6.1, 2. <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> But that the Ministers of the Gospel should be im<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ployed, or might be imployed in them, doth not appear by the Apostle; nay 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 6.4. he speaks the contrary, <ns0:hi>set them to Iudge who are least esteemed in the Church.</ns0:hi> These surely were not the Elders in it. Under the <ns0:hi>Romans,</ns0:hi> the Jews had more liberty, having Civil Courts made up of Persons of their own Religion, to whom our Saviour turns over this Man; being not willing to move out of his Calling, as a Minister of the Gospel. As Christ's Commissioners it is most certain, that no Mi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nisters of the Gospel can intermeddle in Civil Judgments; whether those who are such Commissioners of Christ may yet as Mens Commissioners act, it stands those in Hand who are Ambitious of such an Employment, and can find leisure enough for it<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and are called to it, to inquire I shall not intermeddle in that Controversy. To me, the proper Work of the Gospel is Work enough.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:310" />15 And he said unto them, Take heed, and beware of covetousness, for a mans life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth.<ns0:note place="bottom">The <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> here Translated <ns0:hi>Covetousness,</ns0:hi> is an immode<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rate desire of having of this Worlds Goods, which discovers it self either by unrighteous Acts in procuring, or uncharitable omissions for the keeping of the things of this Life. It is that <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, Love of Money, which the Apostle determineth to be the root of all Evil. It is also discovered by a too much thought<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fulness, what we shall Eat, Drink, or put on, or by the too great meltings of our Hearts into our bags of Gold, or Silver. All these come under the notion of that <ns0:hi>Covetousness,</ns0:hi> which is here for<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bidden. In short, whatsoever it is that hindreth our Contentment with the Portion God giveth us upon our indeavours, though it amounteth to no more than <ns0:hi>Food,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Rayment,</ns0:hi> according to the Apostles Precept, 1 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 6.8. <ns0:hi>& Heb.</ns0:hi> 13.5. This is what Christ warneth his Disciples to beware of, he gives us the rea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />son. <ns0:hi>For Mans Life consisteth not in the abundance of what he possesseth.</ns0:hi> Which is true, whether we understand by Life, the subsisting and upholding of our Life, or (as <ns0:hi>Life</ns0:hi> is often taken) for the <ns0:hi>Happiness and Felicity of our Lives.</ns0:hi> Abun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dance is not necessary to uphold our Lives. <ns0:hi>Ad manum est quod sat est,</ns0:hi> saith <ns0:hi>Seneca,</ns0:hi> Nature is content with a little. <ns0:hi>Sudamus</ns0:hi> (saith he) <ns0:hi>ad supervacanea.</ns0:hi> We sweat only to get Superflui<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ties. Nor will <ns0:hi>abundance</ns0:hi> protect our Lives, it will not keep off an Enemy, but rather tempt him; nor fence out a Disease, but rather contribute to it, as ingaging us in immoderate Cares or La<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bours to procure, and keep it, or as exposing us to Temptations to Riot, and Debauchery, by which Mens Lives are often short<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ned. Nor doth the <ns0:hi>Happiness of Life</ns0:hi> lye in the <ns0:hi>abundance</ns0:hi> of what we possess. Some Philosophers determined rightly, that something of this Worlds good, is necessary to our <ns0:hi>Happiness of Life,</ns0:hi> but <ns0:hi>abundance</ns0:hi> is not. The Poor are as Merry, and many times more satisfyed, more healthy, and at more ease, than those that have abundance. It is a Golden Sentence which deserves to be Ingraven in every Soul.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 And he spake a parable unto them, saying, The ground of a certain rich man brought forth plen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tifully.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 And he thought within himself, saying, What shall I do, because I have no room where to bestow my fruits?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 And he said, This will I do, I will pull down my barns, and build greater, and there will I bestow all my fruits and my goods.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 And I will say to my soul, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Eccl. 11.9, 10. 1 Cor. 15.32. Jam. 5.5.</ns0:note> Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years, take thine ease, eat, drink, <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> be merry.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 But God said unto him, Thou fool! this night shall <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>do they require thy Soul.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Job 20.22. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 27.8. Psal. 52.7.</ns0:note> thy soul be required of thee, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 39.6. Jer. 17.11.</ns0:note> then whose shall those things be which thou hast provided?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 So <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> he that layeth up treasure for himself, and is not rich towards God.<ns0:note place="bottom">The Evangelist lets us know, that these Verses contain not a <ns0:hi>Narrative</ns0:hi> of a matter of Fact, but only a Representation of something that is too ordinary, by a Fictitious Story. The Scope of it is to justify, what our Saviour had said in the Verse imme<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />diately preceding, <ns0:hi>That a Mans Life lyeth not in the abundance of what he possesseth,</ns0:hi> for he who hath the greatest Possessions, may dye as soon as he who hath not where to lay down his Head, and may be taken away, at a time when he is injoying the ful<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lest Satisfactions that he can promise himself, or the Creature can afford him. Therefore he acteth not like a Wise and Rational Man, that takes care to lay up for himself Treasure on Earth, and in the mean time neglecteth the <ns0:hi>Riches of Grace.</ns0:hi> The Sense of the <ns0:hi>Parable</ns0:hi> is to be learned from the <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> which we have <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 21. <ns0:hi>So is he that layeth up Treasure for himself.</ns0:hi> So foolish, and unwise is he, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> But from this Parable we may make general Observations. 1. That God maketh his Sun to shine, and his Rain to fall on the just, and on the unjust. Men may have laid up much Earthly Treasure, who are yet very Poor towards God. 2. That the Increase of Riches inceaseth care. The Rich Man saith, <ns0:hi>What shall I do</ns0:hi>? the difference betwixt the <ns0:hi>Begger</ns0:hi> and the Rich Man is but this, both are saying, <ns0:hi>What shall I do</ns0:hi>? The Begger saith, <ns0:hi>What shall I do to get Money,</ns0:hi> the other saith, <ns0:hi>What shall I do with it now I have it</ns0:hi>? 3. <ns0:hi>World<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly Mens Fruits, are their Goods. v.</ns0:hi> 3. they are so in their Estimation, and they are so as they are the whole Portion, that such should have from God. 4. Great Estates and Enjoyments of this Life, have a very inticing Quality in them, they make us loth to dye, and willing to think we shall live many years. 2. They intice us to a spiritual Sloth and Security, and to Sing a <ns0:hi>Requie<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>
                     </ns0:hi> to our Souls. 3. They intice us to sinful Mirth and Luxury, <ns0:hi>Eat, Drink and be Merry.</ns0:hi> 5. He that hath most, may have his Soul taken from him in a Night. 6. A Man is no longer owner of the Goods of this Life, than he can keep an Earthly Possession of them. 7. When he dyes, he knoweth not whose those things shall be, not whether <ns0:hi>his Son</ns0:hi> or Strangers shall In<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />herit them, nor if his Son doth happen to meet with the Coun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tenance of the Law, doth he know whether that Son shall be a wise Man or a Fool. 8. Hence it appears to be the most Egregious Folly imaginable, for Men to spend their time, and strength in getting, and laying up Treasure upon Earth, in the mean time neglecting, or not duly indeavouring to be <ns0:hi>Rich towards God.</ns0:hi> Both 1. in that Grace by which the Soul is justifyed, and accepted, 2. and also in that <ns0:hi>Grace</ns0:hi> in the Exercise of which alone he may glorify God; this latter is that which the Apostle calls, 1 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 6.18. a <ns0:hi>being Rich in good Works, ready to distribute, willing to Communicate,</ns0:hi> &c. where he mentioneth only one <ns0:hi>Species</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>good Works.</ns0:hi> For whereas Wisdom lies in the choice of the best end, and then of the best means to obtain it, and the best Circumstan<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ces, in the use of those means, the worldly Man failing in the first, not chusing the <ns0:hi>best end</ns0:hi> must needs be a <ns0:hi>Spiritual Fool.</ns0:hi> And indeed, of all <ns0:hi>Folly</ns0:hi> that is the greatest, which is seen in the choice of a worser, and more ignoble end, before that which is of more advantage, more noble, and excellent, as certainly the acquiring of an eternal happiness and Felicity, is before an acquiring a meer Transitory, and incertain felicity and satisfaction.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 And he said unto his disciples, Therefore I say unto you, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 55.22. 1 Pet. 5.7.</ns0:note> Take no thought for your life, what ye shall eat; neither for the body, what ye shall put on.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 The life is more then meat, and the body <ns0:hi>is more</ns0:hi> then raiment.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 Consider the ravens, for they neither sow nor reap, which neither have store-house nor barn, and God feedeth them: How much more are ye better then the fowls.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25 And which of you with taking thought can add to his stature one cubit.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26 If ye then be not able to do that thing which is least, why take ye thought for the rest?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">27 Consider the lilies how they grow: They toyl not, they spin not, and yet I say unto you, that Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">28 If then God so clothe the grass, which is to day in the field, and to morrow is cast into the oven, how much more <ns0:hi>will he cloth</ns0:hi> you, O ye of little faith?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">29 And seek not ye what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink, neither be <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>live no<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> in careful sus<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pence.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> ye of doubtful mind.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="30">30 For all these things do the nations of the world seek after, and your father knoweth that ye have need of these things.<ns0:note place="bottom">See the Notes on <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 6. from <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 25. to <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 33. where we before met with all that is here. The <ns0:hi>thoughtfulness</ns0:hi> here forbid<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />den, is not <ns0:hi>moderate prudent thoughtfulness,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>care,</ns0:hi> but 1. A <ns0:hi>distrustful thoughtfulness.</ns0:hi> 2. <ns0:hi>Distracting or dividing Cares</ns0:hi>; such as make a Man live in suspense, and to be wavering as a Me<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />teor, <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> or, 3. A <ns0:hi>thoughtfulness for high things,</ns0:hi> as some Interpret that Word: But possibly it better signifies such a thoughtfulness to be forbidden, as keeps the mind of Man from rest, in a continual <ns0:hi>motion</ns0:hi> and Fluctuation, or 4. Any <ns0:hi>such thoughtfulness,</ns0:hi> as is <ns0:hi>inconsistent with our seeking first the Kingdom of God.</ns0:hi> Against this thoughtfulness, our Lord Arms his Disciples, with the consideration, 1. Of <ns0:hi>their dependance on God necessarily for their Lives,</ns0:hi> which are better than Meat and Rayment, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 23.2, Of the <ns0:hi>Providence of God,</ns0:hi> which extend<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing to all orders of Creatures, particularly to such as <ns0:hi>meerly have Life</ns0:hi> (such are Vegetables, the <ns0:hi>Grass,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Flowers</ns0:hi>) and <ns0:hi>such as have only Life and Sense</ns0:hi> (such are the Ravens) it cannot be reasonably presumed, that it will be wanting <ns0:hi>to Men,</ns0:hi> who are the most noble order of Sublunary Creatures, having <ns0:hi>being, Life, Sense</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Reason</ns0:hi> (which is the Image of God in Man) 3. From the consideration of the <ns0:hi>Vanity of this care,</ns0:hi> by which we cannot Contribute a <ns0:hi>Cubit to our Stature.</ns0:hi> 4. From the con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sideration that <ns0:hi>the Heathens make these things their care,</ns0:hi> whom Christians ought to excel as knowing more, and living under more excellent hopes and promises then they have. <ns0:hi>Lastly,</ns0:hi> from the consideration of <ns0:hi>their Relation to God as a Father,</ns0:hi> and their <ns0:hi>Fathers knowing</ns0:hi> what they have need of, of whom therefore it were unreasonable to presume, that he should suffer them to want what is necessary for his Children. See more in the <ns0:hi>Notes</ns0:hi> before mentioned on <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 6.25.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="31">31 But rather seek ye the kingdom of God, and all these things shall be added unto you.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>seek first the Kingdom of God, and the Righteousness thereof, and these things shall be added,</ns0:hi> &c. The particle <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> prefixed here to <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> (which we Translate <ns0:hi>Rather seek</ns0:hi>) doth expound <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi>'s <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, <ns0:hi>first seek,</ns0:hi> and likewise Expounds our Saviours meaning, when he said, <ns0:hi>Take no thought, what you should Eat,</ns0:hi> &c. That is, let not those be your only or principal thoughts, <ns0:hi>Quin etiam, tantum maxime.</ns0:hi> But also, and mostly, or chiefly, seek ye the <ns0:hi>Kingdom of God,</ns0:hi> that Kingdom mentioned in the next Verse, and <ns0:hi>all these things shall be added to you,</ns0:hi> either an <ns0:hi>Affluence of them</ns0:hi>; or a suf<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ficiency of them, with a contented satisfyed mind. See more in the Notes on <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 6.33.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="32">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:311" />32 Fear not little flock; <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mat. 11.25, 26.</ns0:note> for it is your Fathers good pleasure to give you the kingdom.<ns0:note place="bottom">Our Saviour had mentioned <ns0:hi>a Kingdom, v.</ns0:hi> 31. How much too big a thought was this for Fisher-men, and others of his poor Hearers to entertain? he therefore here assureth them of the thing, that they should have a <ns0:hi>Kingdom,</ns0:hi> and sheweth them that their Title to it was his and their <ns0:hi>Fathers Will,</ns0:hi> tho they were a <ns0:hi>little Flock,</ns0:hi> and so not like to Conquer a Kingdom upon Earth for themselves, yet they should have a Kingdom from the free Donation of him, who had Kingdoms to give, and would give it to them, because he was their Father. By this Kingdom can be understood nothing else, but that state of Honour, Glory and Dignity, which Believers shall have in the World that is to come, which they shall have not from <ns0:hi>Merit</ns0:hi> but Gift, not from the first good Motions, and Inclinations of their own Will, but from the free motions of the Divine Will, and therefore they had no reason to fear that God would not provide Food convenient for them. He that had provided a Kingdom for them, which he would one Day give unto them, would certainly provide Bread for them, and give it to them.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="33">33 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Acts 2.45. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 4.34.</ns0:note> Sell that ye have, and give alms, provide your selves bags which wax not old, a treasure in the heavens that faileth not, where no thief approach<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth, neither moth corrupteth.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="34">34 For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.<ns0:note place="bottom">The immutable purpose of the Divine Being to Glorify the Disciples of Christ, The freedom of the Divine Will, in the Gift of Heaven and Glory, are neither of them exclusive of, but in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />clude, and suppose their Duty to use such due Means, as he hath directed them, in the use of which they shall obtain, what he hath purposed for them, and promised to them. Some of which are here directed and prescribed. <ns0:hi>Sell that you have, and give Alms,</ns0:hi> &c. It is a precept of the same import with that, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 19.21. <ns0:hi>Mar.</ns0:hi> 10.21. Tho possibly, The Precept here given to the Dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ciples of Christ, generally is not to be interpreted, so strictly as seemeth to be our Saviour's meaning in those Texts, as to the young Man. For it seems to have been a special Precept to him, laying an Obligation upon him to make a present <ns0:hi>Actual Sale</ns0:hi> of all he had, and it is plain that he so understood it. To this Christians are not obliged generally by this precept. 1. But to be ready at the call and command of God to part with all, for such uses as God should shew them: not to set their Heart on Riches, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 62.10. to be ready to distribute, and willing to Communicate, 1 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 6.18. remembring that God <ns0:hi>loveth Mercy rather then Sacrifice, Hos.</ns0:hi> 6.6. <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 9.13. To give of our <ns0:hi>Superflui<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ties, Luke</ns0:hi> 3.11. To make Friends of our <ns0:hi>Mammon of unrigh<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />teousness, Luke</ns0:hi> 16.9. Nay if the necessities of the People of God be such as requires it, for the subsistence of Christians, to <ns0:hi>sell what we have,</ns0:hi> rather than others of Gods People should starve, calling nothing our own in such a case, which Christians did in the Primitive State of the Church, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 4.34, 35.37. For the other part of <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 33. and <ns0:hi>v</ns0:hi> 34. see the Notes on <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 6.20, 21.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="35">35 Let your loyns be girded about, and <ns0:hi>your</ns0:hi> lights burning.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="36">36 And ye your selves like unto men that wait for their Lord, when he will return from the wed<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ding, that when he cometh and knocketh, they may o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pen unto him immediately.<ns0:note place="bottom">The first Words of the fortieth Verse expound the thirty fifth<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 
                     <ns0:hi>Be ye therefore always ready also.</ns0:hi> In this Sense we find the Phrase used, 1 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 18.46. 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 4.29. <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 9.1. <ns0:hi>Iob</ns0:hi> 38.3. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 40.7. <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 1.17. In those Eastern Countries, both Masters, and Ser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vants were wont to wear long Garments, which they were wont to <ns0:hi>Gird up,</ns0:hi> either when they went to <ns0:hi>Fight,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>when they were to Travel, Exod.</ns0:hi> 12.11. 1 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 18.46. or <ns0:hi>when they went about any Service,</ns0:hi> see <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 17.8. <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 13.4. this was a piece of their Preparation. We read of the <ns0:hi>Girding about of the Loyns of the mind with Truth, Eph.</ns0:hi> 6.14. and with habits of Grace and Vertue, 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 1.13. wherefore <ns0:hi>Gird up the Loyns of your minds, be sober,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>hope to the end.</ns0:hi> The other Phrase, <ns0:hi>and your Lights burning</ns0:hi> is of the same import, relating to the Lords <ns0:hi>coming from the Wedding,</ns0:hi> mentioned <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 36. For in those Countries, their Weddings were celebrated in the Night. Christ is coming to Judgment, whether our particular, or the more <ns0:hi>ge<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />neral Iudgment,</ns0:hi> is that, which is here set out to us, under the no<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion of a Mans coming home late at Night from a Wedding. Nor improperly, for in this Life Souls are united to Christ, <ns0:hi>Eph.</ns0:hi> 5<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 32. when Christ shall have done his Work of that Nature upon the Earth, that all the Elect shall be gathered, then shall he come to Judge the World. He would have all his People be ready for that Day, and waiting for their Lord, that his coming may be welcome to them.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="37">37 Blessed <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> those servants, whom the Lord when he cometh shall find watching: verily I say unto you, that he shall gird himself, and make them to sit down to meat, and will come forth and serve them.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="38">38 And if he shall come in the second watch, or come in the third watch, and find <ns0:hi>them</ns0:hi> so, blessed are those servants.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="39">39 And this know, that if the good man of the house had known what hour the thief would come, he would have watched, and not have suffered his house to be broken through.</ns0:p>

Chap. 21.34. 1 Thess. 5.6.</ns0:note> Be ye therefore ready also, for the Son of man cometh at an hour when ye think not.<ns0:note place="bottom">The Duty which Christ is here pressing upon his hearers, is a <ns0:hi>Watchfulness,</ns0:hi> which signifyeth, 1. A Negation of Sleep, 2. An Industrious keeping our selves awake with reference to some particular end. The end here expressed, to be the happy recei<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ving of Christ, coming to judgment from whence is evident, that the Watching he<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>e intended, is a <ns0:hi>Spiritual Watching,</ns0:hi> which is a denial of our selves as to our <ns0:hi>Lusts,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Sleep of Sin,</ns0:hi> which is compared to <ns0:hi>Sleep, Rom.</ns0:hi> 13.11. <ns0:hi>Eph.</ns0:hi> 5.14. and an Industrious keeping our selves from such Sleep in order to the coming of our Lord. Who will come, at an Hour when <ns0:hi>we think not, v.</ns0:hi> 40. His coming is to us incertain, and will be to many <ns0:hi>Surprizing.</ns0:hi> This Watchfulness he presseth upon his Hearers, 1. <ns0:hi>From the reward the Lord will give to such Persons. He shall Gird himself, and make them sit down to Meat, and will come forth and serve them.</ns0:hi> Very high Metaphorical Expres<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sions, signifying no more, than that he will put upon them a <ns0:hi>very high Honour and Dignity,</ns0:hi> and satisfy them with a fulness of Happiness and Glory, and they shall be at Rest for ever. The State of Glory is elsewhere set out under the notion of <ns0:hi>drinking new Wine in the Kingdom of God,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Eating and Drinking in his Kingdom.</ns0:hi> 2. From the <ns0:hi>Benefit</ns0:hi> which they will have by Watching in this. That let the Lord come when he will, whe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther in the <ns0:hi>Second</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Third Watch,</ns0:hi> they will be ready, and they shall be Blessed. 3. He presseth it also from the ordinary Prudence of Men, who if they have an intimation, that a <ns0:hi>Thief</ns0:hi> is com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing, will Watch, and prevent the mischief that might ensue by the breaking open of their Houses. But concerning those Words, see the Notes on <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 24.43. where we met with them be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore used upon the same occasion.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>

                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> Who then is that faith<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ful and wise steward, whom <ns0:hi>his</ns0:hi> lord shall make ru<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ler over his houshold, to give <ns0:hi>them their</ns0:hi> portion of meat in due season.</ns0:p>

               <ns0:p n="47">47 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Jam. 4.17.</ns0:note> that servant which knew his lords will, and prepared not <ns0:hi>himself,</ns0:hi> neither did according to his will, shall be beaten with many <ns0:hi>stripes,</ns0:hi>

               <ns0:p n="48">48 But he that knew not, and did commit things worthy of stripes, shall be beaten with few <ns0:hi>stripes.</ns0:hi> For unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required, and to whom men have committed much, of him they will ask the more.<ns0:note place="bottom">See the Notes on <ns0:hi>Matth,</ns0:hi> 24. from <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 45. to the end, where we met with thesame Parable, but here expressed more largely, and with more Circumstances. <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> hath not the Introduction to it, which we have here, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 41. Doth this Duty of <ns0:hi>Watchfulness</ns0:hi> concern all thy Disciples, or only us, that are thine Apostles, the Ministers of thy Gospel? The substance of what our Lord saith in Answer to <ns0:hi>Peter,</ns0:hi> from <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 42. to <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 49. is. <ns0:hi>Peter,</ns0:hi> I spake it to all, I have not the meanest Hearer, but is concerned to <ns0:hi>Watch</ns0:hi> against my coming.                <ns0:p n="49">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:311" />49 I am come to send fire on the earth, and what will I, if it be already kindled?<ns0:note place="bottom">Some of the ancients here by <ns0:hi>Fire,</ns0:hi> understood the <ns0:hi>Holy Ghost,</ns0:hi> or the <ns0:hi>Preaching of the Gospel,</ns0:hi> with those <ns0:hi>Flames of Love,</ns0:hi> and holy affections which that causeth in the hearts of good People, but this Interpretation cannot but be looked upon as strained to those who compare this verse with <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 51, 52, 53. and the Parallel Text in <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 10.34, 35, 36. by <ns0:hi>Fire</ns0:hi> here therefore is to be understood the <ns0:hi>dissension,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>division</ns0:hi> mentioned <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 15. with all those Persecutions, Wars, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> which are the effects of it. A Prediction, or threatning of Persecutions, or Wars, or any kind of troubled State of things is often expressed in Holy Writ under the notion of <ns0:hi>Fire,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Water,</ns0:hi> or a <ns0:hi>Flood,</ns0:hi> for though Fire and Water are opposite in their qualities, yet they both agree in the common effect of consumption, wasting and desolation. Christ saith, <ns0:hi>he came to find it,</ns0:hi> because he foresaw this would be a certain consequent, tho not a proper and natural effect of the Preaching of the Gospel. Christ may be said to come to <ns0:hi>send a Fire</ns0:hi> in the same sense, as he that is imployed in the removal of a filthy Dung<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hill, may be said <ns0:hi>to come to send a stench,</ns0:hi> his design is to carry the muck away, and in a due time he will have done it, but in the mean time it sends out a much greater stench then before it was stirred. <ns0:hi>And what will I? if it be already kindled?</ns0:hi> not to take notice of what critical Authors say, about the signification of the Particles, or the Phrase here used, I take the true sense to be, <ns0:hi>I desire nothing more then that it were already kindled,</ns0:hi> nor was this anymore inconsistent with the Goodness and Holiness of Christ, then for a Gold-Smith to wish the Fire was kindled that should separate the dross from the pure Mettal, or then for Christ to de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sire that <ns0:hi>his floor</ns0:hi> were <ns0:hi>throughly Purged.</ns0:hi> Christ doth not desire the <ns0:hi>Fire</ns0:hi> for the <ns0:hi>Fires sake,</ns0:hi> but for the sake of that effect it would have, in separating in his Church the good from the bad; it was a thing he saw would be through the opposition the World would give to the Preaching of the Gospel, before his Gospel would ob<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tain in the World; I would, saith he, that what they do, they would do quickly, that they would spit their Venome, that my <ns0:hi>Father</ns0:hi> might make their Wrath to praise him, whereas some interprete it indicatively, as if the Fire were already begun <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> can hardly be so Interpreted.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="50">50 But I have a baptism to be baptized with, and how am I straitned till it be accomplished?<ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>pained.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note place="bottom">This <ns0:hi>Baptism</ns0:hi> spoken of here by our Saviour is the same men<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tioned <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 20.22, 23. and can be understood of nothing but his Passion, the accomplishment of which he hinteth us was to be, before the Fire (before mentioned) would blaze up on the Earth. Concerning this he saith he was <ns0:hi>straitned till it was accomplished</ns0:hi>; not that he willed the influencing of the heart of <ns0:hi>Iudas</ns0:hi> to betray him, the heart of <ns0:hi>Pilate</ns0:hi> to condemn him, or the hearts of the wicked Jews, to accuse, Condemn and Crucifie him, but he <ns0:hi>willed these events,</ns0:hi> for the manifestation of the Glory of his Father, in the Redemption of the World by him<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> As the Woman big with Child heartily wisheth that the hour of her <ns0:hi>Travel</ns0:hi> were come and over, not for the <ns0:hi>pains sake,</ns0:hi> which she must endure, but for her own ease sake, and the joy she should have of a Child born into the World.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="51">51 Suppose ye that I am come to give peace on earth? I tell you, Nay, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mic. 7.6.</ns0:note> but rather division.</ns0:p>

               <ns0:p n="53">53 The father shall be divided against the son, and the son against the father: the mother against the daughter, and the daughter against the mother: the mother in law, against her daughter in law, and the daughter in law, against her mother in law.<ns0:note place="bottom">See the <ns0:hi>Notes</ns0:hi> on <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 10.34, 35.                <ns0:p n="56">56 Ye hypocrites, ye can discern the face of the skie, and of the earth: but how is it, that ye do not discern this time?<ns0:note place="bottom">We met with a discourse of the same Nature <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 16.2.                <ns0:p n="57">57 Yea, and why even of your selves judge ye not what is right?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="58">58 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Prov. 25.8.</ns0:note> When thou goest with thine adversary to the magistrate, <ns0:hi>as thou art</ns0:hi> in the way, give diligence that thou mayest be delivered from him; lest he hale thee to the judge, and the judge deliver thee to the officer, and the officer cast thee into prison.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="59">59 I tell thee, thou shalt not depart thence till thou hast paid the very last mite <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                     <ns0:hi>See</ns0:hi> Mark 12.42.</ns0:note>.<ns0:note place="bottom">Our Saviour made use of this expression, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 5.25. to per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />swade Peace betwixt Brethren, here he useth it to perswade Men to <ns0:hi>acquaint themselves with God, and be at Peace.</ns0:hi> He had been treating of the last Judgment, there was no fitter foundation, upon which he could build an exhortation to <ns0:hi>Repentance,</ns0:hi> and making our Peace with God. In not doing of it, he telleth his hearers that they did not <ns0:hi>of themselves judge what was right,</ns0:hi> for if they did, they would judge themselves as much concerned to come to an agreement with God, as they did ordinarily to come to an agreement with Men.
